sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Willingboro?
sections.html:
Willingboro requires a township certificate of occupancy before any change of ownership, and the inspection has to be booked at least 15 days before settlement. Everything else follows from that clock: heating certification, repairs, reinspection and the deed filing in Mount Holly.

The township is a Burlington County suburb of Philadelphia with 32,824 residents and one of the most affordable owner markets in this part of New Jersey. Below are the figures, the resale rules and the tax steps that apply to a Willingboro sale, followed by a comparison of listing, selling on your own and taking an as-is cash offer.

sections.h2: How does the Willingboro housing market look on paper?
sections.html:
Willingboro grew out of a single builder's plan, and the numbers still show it: 84.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, households average 3.02 people, and the township covers 7.73 square miles of land with about 4,128 residents per square mile. The 2020 census counted 31,889 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 32,824.

sections.h2: What is the Levittown story behind Willingboro's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Willingboro began as the Constabulary of Wellingborrow on November 6, 1688, and was incorporated as a township on February 21, 1798. Its present shape comes from the 1950s and 1960s, when Levitt and Sons built its third and largest Levittown here. The first homes sold in June 1958, and the population climbed from 852 in 1950 to 43,386 in 1970.

The township even carried the Levittown name from 1959 until a referendum on November 5, 1963 restored Willingboro. The planning left a pattern buyers still use to find a house:

  • Neighborhoods are called parks, such as Pennypacker Park, Millbrook Park, Windsor Park and Hawthorne Park.
  • Streets inside each park start with the same letter as the park's name, so a Pennypacker address starts with P.
  • Country Club Ridge was laid out in the 1960s around a Robert Trent Jones golf course.
  • Pennypacker Park and Country Club Park hold the community pools.

Because so many houses came from a handful of floor plans, appraisers and buyers compare your house with the same model a few streets away. Knowing your model, its additions and when the roof and heating were last replaced helps a price hold up.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools matter to Willingboro buyers?
sections.html:
U.S. Route 130 forms the northwest edge of the township, and Rancocas Creek drains the southwest side. Willingboro borders Burlington Township, Delanco, Delran, Edgewater Park, Moorestown, Mount Laurel and Westampton. Of its 122.11 miles of roads, 109.02 miles are township-maintained.

Transit is by bus. NJ Transit routes 409, 417 and 418 run between Trenton and Philadelphia, BurLink runs two local routes, and Academy Bus links Willingboro to Midtown and Lower Manhattan.

Willingboro Township Public Schools has nine schools and 3,456 students as of 2020-21. Hawthorne, W.R. James Sr. and Twin Hills serve grades 1 to 4, Levitt Intermediate covers grades 5 and 6, Memorial Middle School covers 7 and 8, and Willingboro High School covers 9 to 12. A buyer with children will check the school assigned to your park, so have that answer ready.

sections.h2: What certificate of occupancy does Willingboro require to sell?
sections.html:
Willingboro's housing standards chapter requires a certificate of occupancy before a change in ownership or occupancy of any dwelling, issued by the township's Department of Inspections. The steps from the ordinance run in this order:

  • The owner or agent applies and pays the fee set in the township fee schedule.
  • The inspection must be scheduled at least 15 calendar days before the settlement date, and a request made four or fewer days out adds an $80 expedite fee.
  • Canceling or moving the appointment takes 24 hours' notice, or the first fee is charged anyway.
  • The inspector makes a visual check of accessible parts of the structure, which is not a guarantee of electrical, plumbing or heating systems.
  • A qualified technician authorized by the township must separately certify the heating equipment, and that certification can be no more than 30 days old when the certificate issues.
  • A failed inspection produces a written notice of defects, and the owner has 30 days from the inspection date to repair and request reinspection.

The township now takes resale and rental applications through an online citizen portal. A buyer may agree to take on repairs at closing, but the township still treats the certificate as the seller's task unless your contract says otherwise, so put the responsibility in writing.

sections.h2: How are the deed and state transfer fee handled in Willingboro?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Burlington County Clerk's main office at 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The clerk's website also lists a Property Fraud Alert service, which you can use to watch for any document filed in your name.

Seller paperwork has a recent change. The county says GIT/REP seller tax declarations signed on or after October 1, 2025 must be on the newest state form, and older versions are rejected. Questions about the form go to the state Division of Taxation.

On a sale of $350,000 or less, the state realty transfer fee is $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000, and $3.90 per $500 from $200,000 to $350,000. At a $270,300 price, that works out to roughly $1,070 on the first $150,000 plus a few hundred dollars more for the remainder; your closing agent will give the exact figure.

sections.h2: When are Willingboro property taxes due, and what is the tax sale?
sections.html:
Willingboro bills taxes on the calendar year, with payments due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, plus a 10-day grace period. On the eleventh day, interest is figured back to the first, and the township does not accept postmarks.

Taxes can be paid at the tax office window in the municipal building, in the Police Department drop box, by mail or online. The tax office is at One Rev. Dr. M. L. King Jr. Drive, Suite 205, and its window hours are 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Online payment of prior-year taxes is not allowed, so ask the collector for the exact payoff amount before closing.

Any balance still open after December 31 goes into the township's electronic tax sale, held each October for unpaid prior-year taxes and municipal charges. The 2026 sale was set for October 14. For senior, veteran or disabled-person deductions, the assessor's office at 609-877-2200 takes the applications.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Willingboro?
sections.html:
A listing can fetch the strongest price on a clean house, a cash offer removes the inspection cycle, and selling on your own sits in between. The 15-day inspection rule makes timing the main difference.

  • Listing suits a house in good repair, since a buyer's lender will want the heating certified and the township certificate in hand.
  • A sale on your own suits an owner who knows the neighborhood's recent prices and will hire an attorney for the contract.
  • An as-is cash purchase suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate, because the buyer can take on the defect list.

Whichever you choose, schedule the township inspection when you set the closing date, not after, and compare offers by the amount that reaches you after the transfer fee, taxes and mortgage payoff.

faqs.q: Does Willingboro require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The township requires a certificate of occupancy before a change in ownership, and the inspection must be scheduled at least 15 calendar days before settlement. A heating equipment certification from a qualified technician is also required.

faqs.q: What happens if my Willingboro house fails the inspection?
faqs.a: The Department of Inspections issues a written notice of defects. You then have 30 days from the inspection to complete repairs and ask for a reinspection, after which the certificate is issued.
February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a 10-day grace period. The township does not honor postmarks, and balances open after December 31 enter the October tax sale.

faqs.q: Where is a Willingboro deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Burlington County Clerk's main office, 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Willingboro house with tenants or repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate rules still apply, but an as-is buyer can agree to take over the defect list and the occupancy. Put the responsibility for the inspection and any repairs in the written contract.
